findings.description: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT (line 1069) names only the policy-check.yml + release-gate.yml assertion-string sites: 'Search for `assert yaml.__version__ ==` and `assert jsonschema.__version__ ==` across `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` and `.github/workflows/release-gate.yml`.' Slice 020N adds a THIRD workflow with hardcoded version-pin assertions — `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` (`assert yaml.__version__ == '6.0.3'`, `assert jsonschema.__version__ == '4.26.0'`, `assert fastapi.__version__ == '0.136.1'`, `assert pydantic.VERSION == '2.13.3'`). A maintainer following the §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT procedure when bumping pyyaml or jsonschema would search only the two named files and miss the conflict-gate.yml assertions. The `requirements/conflict-gate.in` carries its own REGENERATION INVARIANT callout pointing to conflict-gate.yml — so the per-lockfile documentation IS present — but §12.7.13 remains the canonical SCP-internal supply-chain posture reference and an operator who reads only that document would overlook the conflict-gate.yml assertion sites.
findings.recommendation: Extend the REGENERATION INVARIANT callout in ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 to name `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` alongside `policy-check.yml` and `release-gate.yml`. The search should cover all three files. The TF-020M-002 prune in this slice correctly notes that the inline REGENERATION INVARIANT in §12.7.13 covers the lockstep concern — but it currently covers only the policy-check/release-gate pair. The gap is: conflict-gate has its own lockfile (conflict-gate.txt) and its own assertion strings (pyyaml 6.0.3, jsonschema 4.26.0, fastapi 0.136.1, pydantic 2.13.3) that are NOT mentioned in §12.7.13. File as a new TF (TF-020N-001) if not addressable in this slice. Acceptable as a fast-follow since §12.7.13 is SCP-internal posture documentation, not adopter-facing guidance.
findings.rationale: §12.7.13 is the canonical SCP internal supply-chain posture reference. The REGENERATION INVARIANT is expressly designed to prevent lockstep failures. With three lockfiles (policy-check.txt, release-gate via policy-check.txt, conflict-gate.txt) and three assertion-string sites, the invariant must enumerate all three or it will be incomplete as a maintenance guard. Per exam item (5): adopters do not consume conflict-gate.yml, so this is NOT an adopter-disclosure gap — it is a SCP-internal maintenance documentation gap.

findings.description: The DISPATCH-NOTE §'Internal-surface justification (no semver bump)' quotes the VERSIONING.md §'Scope' exclusion list verbatim: 'It does NOT cover internal-only surfaces: `lib/policy_check_invocation.sh`, `scripts/scp-policy-check.lock`, helper scripts in `scripts/`, the Renovate preset internal shape, or the OPA Rego `scp_common.rego` helpers.' The no-semver-bump justification is by-omission: `conflict-gate.yml` is not in the positive public-surface enumeration (workflow_call.inputs on policy-check.yml, schema contracts, rule IDs), and is not explicitly mentioned in the exclusion list. The DISPATCH-NOTE correctly frames this as 'not in the public surface enumerated by VERSIONING.md §"Scope"' rather than 'explicitly excluded'. The D-039 decision row mirrors this framing. Per exam item (6): the by-omission framing is technically correct but the exclusion list in VERSIONING.md §'Scope' is a positive enumeration of examples, not an exhaustive exclusion list. An auditor reading VERSIONING.md alone could ask: 'Where does .github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml fit?' The exclusion list's examples are all from non-.github paths; no `.github/workflows/**` file is named.
findings.recommendation: Cosmetic only. VERSIONING.md §'Scope' could add `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` (or more broadly 'SCP-self-only workflows that are not callable by adopters') to the exclusion list examples, making the by-omission justification explicit. D-039's rationale text already does this well ('SCP-self-only workflow that adopters do not consume') — the gap is that VERSIONING.md itself doesn't enumerate the pattern. A one-line addition like 'SCP-self-only workflows (e.g. `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml`) that are not callable via `workflow_call` by adopters' to the exclusion list would prevent future ambiguity. Non-blocking; file as TF-020N-003 if the operator wants to track it.
findings.rationale: D-039 and the DISPATCH-NOTE are clear; the no-semver-bump justification is well-constructed and by-omission is a valid framing (the positive enumeration doesn't include conflict-gate.yml). The nit is that a future maintainer adding a second SCP-self workflow might wonder whether it needs a version bump; VERSIONING.md's §'Scope' would be cleaner with an explicit SCP-self-workflow pattern. The risk is non-trivial only when estate scale grows beyond single-operator.

findings.description: The DISPATCH-NOTE does not include a post-merge close-out checklist (unlike 020M's DISPATCH-NOTE which had items (x)/(xi) covering the tag-cut, release publication, and post-merge obligations). The absence of a close-out checklist in the DISPATCH-NOTE means the operator has no filed reminder for step (3).

Per exam item (11): the memory update is a close-out task and non-blocking at merge. But the absence of the checklist increases the risk the operator skips step (c).

summary: Slice 020N is a clean and well-scoped post-Threshold-A standalone supply-chain hardening. TF-020M-001 closure is accurate and comprehensive — the STATUS.md description correctly captures the BROADER surface (all PyPI deps, not just pyyaml) and enumerates all four install step restructuring actions. TF-020M-002 prune is correct — the REGENERATION INVARIANT in ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 was already added in fix-round-2 and directly covers the lockstep coupling concern. D-039 is complete, well-positioned chronologically, and symmetric with D-038. All seven DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criteria (i)-(vii) have verifiable file evidence in the diff. CODEOWNERS coverage on requirements/** is confirmed from slice 020M. Cumulative TF state matches the expected open/closed inventory in the package. Two MIN findings require attention: (1) COMP-MIN-001 — ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT names only policy-check.yml + release-gate.yml assertion sites; slice 020N adds a third workflow (conflict-gate.yml) with four hardcoded assertion strings that a maintainer following §12.7.13 would miss; a TF or fast-follow amendment is needed; (2) COMP-MIN-002 — STATUS.md lacks a session chain entry for 020N IN FLIGHT and the DISPATCH-NOTE has no post-merge close-out checklist, creating a risk the operator misses the STATUS.md chain update and memory entry post-merge. Neither finding is a functional defect; both are documentation/governance completeness gaps. Verdict: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS — the two MIN findings should be resolved before or immediately after merge, ideally as a filed TF (TF-020N-001 for the §12.7.13 gap, TF-020N-002 for the close-out checklist).
